first.rationale: Promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. However, the memory does not establish durable retention, margin quality, or long-term qualified revenue, so it should be verified and tested narrowly. Memory 86 is the strongest competing response to the simultaneous onboarding decline and should be verified to compare its downstream revenue evidence before commitment.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning better with sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because its verified cohort had 30-day retention -12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Longer-term revenue impact beyond 30 days remains uncertain, so retain an experimental holdout and track qualified conversion and renewal.
